title: Two On My Vessel blocks asserted things nothing establishes - a fleet-wide cloud-sync backup with an evidentiary standing, and a universal loading-computer module requirement inferred from a corporate fleet profile - and the same card asserted a True Confidence crew fact external verification could not reach
candidate_claim: Tranche 2C sections 1, 2 and 8. QB5_C_B#q5 On My Vessel claims an automated remote cloud-sync backup of critical machinery logs via fleet telemetry, and that this preserves records for international maritime tribunals. QB2_A#q27 On My Vessel presents a Maersk fleet profile as personal experience and asserts that any specialised dry bulk charter requires the loading computer to carry approved IMSBC and Grain modules. Separately, K-2/K-3: True Confidence was a bulk carrier (verified), twenty crew were evacuated by the Indian Navy and three died (verified), but the proposition that the survivor was the sole Indian national aboard is NOT established to the required standard.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON ALL THREE, AND ONE PROPAGATION WAS FOUND THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME. The two On My Vessel defects are the same class - a capability or a requirement asserted at fleet scale from a position that cannot know it - and are corrected together for that reason. On K-2 the barred proposition was live in TWO places, not one: the q5 Casualty Link, and the governed correction-log note for the Q5 v1.1-to-v1.2 entry, which read that the vessel sole Indian crew member (of 20) survived. THE CORRECTION LOG IS A CANDIDATE-FACING PUBLISHED SURFACE, generated into meoclass1/qb_content_index.json. Correcting the card alone would have left the corpus asserting on a published surface exactly the proposition the card had just been made to drop - and it would have passed every digest gate, because the log is not a q-card. The note is corrected to the verified facts and nothing else in it is touched.

authority.cloud_sync: NO SOURCE. The claim is an assertion about a company IT estate and about the evidentiary weight of its output. Nothing in the held corpus establishes either, and no substitute system was invented to replace it. The corrected block asserts only what the surrounding regime already supports and what the card own reg-box already carries: preservation of the ORIGINAL records unaltered, security under the Master authority and the company SMS procedure, a documented chain of custody, and release through the Master to the flag State, the port State and the marine safety investigation Authority. Shore-replicated telemetry is described as system-specific, with its evidentiary status for the company and the investigating authority to establish, and as no substitute for the originals.
authority.loading_computer: NO SOURCE for a universal requirement. Replaced with the Founder preferred wording, which answers from the applicable Grain Code stability criteria and the IMSBC cargo-group framework and says plainly that this is not a routine regime on the ships sailed. No company procedure invented.
authority.true_confidence: K-3 VERIFIED - bulk carrier, per the IMO Red Sea incidents list and CENTCOM. Descriptor added. K-2 PARTLY VERIFIED - three fatalities (two Filipino, one Vietnamese) and twenty survivors evacuated by the Indian Navy are supported by high-authority reporting; the sole Indian national aboard is NOT, and is removed rather than retained with a hedge. Nothing about the fatalities was strengthened.
authority.ism_msc255_split_untouched: The MSC.255(84) / ISM section 9 split lives in the reg-box and the CE Oral Tip. Neither was opened by this correction, and the 15-second and 60-second layers that state the split are byte-identical within the card.

supersedes.note: CORR-GPT-T2A-QB5CB-20260905 corrected the ISM/CIC regime split in this card. It did not open the On My Vessel or Casualty Link blocks.

changed_propositions: On My Vessel: the automated, remote cloud-sync backup for critical machinery logs via fleet telemetry, and its asserted preservation for international maritime tribunals, REMOVED - replaced by preservation of the ORIGINAL records unaltered, protection against alteration, back-dating or loss, security under the Master authority and the company SMS procedure with a documented chain of custody, and availability through the Master to the flag State, the port State and the marine safety investigation Authority; shore-replicated telemetry labelled system-specific and expressly no substitute for the originals.
On My Vessel: damage containment and data security -> damage containment and evidence preservation.
Casualty Link: the merchant vessel True Confidence -> the bulk carrier True Confidence (K-3, verified).

Casualty Link: the vessel sole Indian crew member was among the 20 survivors evacuated by the Indian Navy -> the twenty surviving crew were evacuated by the Indian Navy. The unverified proposition is removed, not hedged.
deliberately_unchanged: The 15-second and 60-second answers, which carry the MSC.255(84) / ISM section 9 split and were not opened.
The reg-box, including the ISM section 9 row that states the split in full, and the CE Oral Tip.

The Casualty Link note for oral delivery, which warns that the question premise of three Indian crew dying is a training scenario not matching the real fatalities. It is the point of the block and is unchanged.
The Numbers / Regs block, including the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 Part XI machinery.
The Trap Warning, CE Relevance, Trap Questions, Common CE Failures and Examiner Chain blocks.

artefacts.why_no_digest: The governed source of the published correction log. A digest here would expire on the next unrelated log entry, so the change is asserted on its CONTENT by validate_correction_gptt2c.py instead - the same rule CORR-GPT-T2A-GRAIN-20260905 applied to known_traps.md.
artefacts.what_changed: The recently_updated note for the QB5_C_B Q5 v1.1-to-v1.2 entry: the clause asserting that the vessel sole Indian crew member (of 20) survived is replaced by the verified statement that the twenty surviving crew were evacuated by the Indian Navy. Nothing else in that note, and no other note, changed.

propagation.scope_pass: Corpus-wide sweep of meoclass1/ for sole Indian, cloud-sync, fleet telemetry and dry bulk charter. Two live sites for the first - the q5 card and the governed correction-log note, the latter surfacing in meoclass1/qb_content_index.json - and one each for the rest. All four corrected. Post-correction the sweep returns zero.

invariants: No new Maersk system, procedure or capability is invented anywhere in this record or in either card.
The evidence-preservation lesson in q5 is not weakened: the corrected block is longer and more specific about what is preserved, from what it is protected, and to whom it is released.
No True Confidence fatality fact is changed, added or strengthened. Only the unverified nationality proposition is removed and the verified ship-type descriptor added.
The q5 warning that the question premise is a training scenario survives verbatim.
QB2_A#q11 and #q33 are not touched by this record.
Corpus totals unmoved: 761 canonical questions across 86 question-bearing files.
meoclass1/index.html is byte-identical; the hub date still reads Last Updated: 2 Sep 2026.
content_index_effect: meoclass1/qb_content_index.json IS regenerated by this correction, and that is the point rather than a side effect: the generator reads the governed note, so the corrected note is what reaches the published correction log. No question id, anchor or question text changed, so the totals and the per-file counts regenerate identically at 761 / 86.
note: SURGICAL. Two cards and one governed log note. The log note is the finding this record would have missed if it had trusted the brief scope: a card-level correction that leaves the same barred proposition live on a generated candidate-facing surface has not removed the claim, it has only moved where a candidate reads it.
